newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Sport7 TV channel under pressure - media.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Sport7 TV channel under pressure - media.

text.p: New Dutch television channel Sport7 received a double blow at the weekend as ING Barings forecast a large full year loss for the company and the Dutch soccer president criticised its venture into pay-TV, in a bundle including a porn channel, the Dutch media said.
Sport7 began broadcasting in August. Most Dutch households can receive it for the standard cable TV fee, but, in and around Amsterdam, it arrives as part of a supplementary pay-TV package.
ING Barings' report on Sport7 forecast a loss of 102 million guilders in the 1996/97 fiscal year, newspaper Het Financieele Dagblad said on Saturday.

The paper quoted ING's report as saying that the channel was suffering from poor audience ratings and large start-up costs. ING said Sport7 needed to link with other commercial channels to form a powerful pay-TV package, but that it will be two years before Dutch cable companies have installed sufficient pay-TV decoders.
Last week, the NOS audience research unit showed that in its first full month of operation, Sport7 gained a four percent share of the Dutch television audience.

In an interview in the NRC-Handelsblad newspaper, the president of the Dutch soccer association, Jos Staatsen, said he was unhappy with the decision by Amsterdam cable company A2000 to launch a "pluspakket" of entertainment channels including Sport7.
"What concerns me is that Sport7 in Amsterdam pulls out of that package as soon as possible. It's a revolting package. Sport7 is being used to shoe-horn the other channels in," Staatsen said.

A2000 Holding NV, which pipes television to households in and around Amsterdam, is a cable TV joint venture between Philips Electronics NV venture and US West. Its pluspakket includes a Chinese entertainment channel CNE and a soft porn channel.
Sport7 has received a battering from the Dutch media since its start in August, but Staatsen was unwilling to write the channel off yet.

"Sport7 has not been on the air for two months yet. Some parts of the media have already sounded its death knell. But the public has not yet had the chance to decide. The stakeholders still have complete faith in the venture," he said.

Sport7 is owned by PTT Nederland ING, Philips Electronics and Dutch TV production firm Endemol (each with 19.5 percent), Dutch soccer association KNVB, with 10 percent and De Telegraaf, with five percent.
